stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read and follow the new material.

blocks.title: Why standards matter
blocks.text: Standards are agreed rules/specifications that allow equipment and software from different manufacturers to communicate.

blocks.title: Protocols in action
blocks.text: A protocol provides rules for exchanging data. Different services need different protocol functions.

blocks.title: Different communication jobs
blocks.text: A web request uses a web protocol such as HTTP/HTTPS. TCP supports reliable ordered delivery, while IP handles addressing and routing.

blocks.title: Layering is an explanation
blocks.text: Communication tasks can be considered in stages/layers. OCR J277 does not require memorising names and functions of all TCP/IP model layers; focus on the required standards and protocol functions.

blocks.title: Worked example
blocks.text: Different manufacturers need compatible rules if their devices are to communicate. Agreed standards [1] help equipment from different makers interoperate [1]. Communication protocols define common rules for sending data [1], so requests can be interpreted correctly by devices [1]. Four points: standard → compatibility, protocol → effective exchange.

items: Standard — Agreed technical specification allowing compatibility.
Protocol — Agreed rules for communication between devices.
Interoperability — Different hardware/software systems working together.
Layering — Separating communication tasks into different functions.
